clue.text: Line made with hair found in a boat

parts.note: a row is a line of things side by side
a lock is a tress or curl of hair

explanation.surface: Someone fashions a fishing line out of hair while out on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The oar rests in this notch or pivot on the gunwale, a fitting every rowing craft carries.

clue.text: Sort of course taken by barrister ?

explanation.surface: A lawyer takes some kind of course.
explanation.walkthrough: A barrister's refresher is an extra fee paid during a long case.
explanation.definitionFit: A short course updating one's skills; and an additional fee paid to counsel.

clue.text: Part of a torpedo in general for example

explanation.surface: A part of a torpedo, as a typical example.
explanation.walkthrough: A general can be called, playfully, a head of war.
explanation.definitionFit: The explosive nose of a missile; and a commander as a chief in battle.

clue.text: Figures in red demonstration ?

parts.note: a bank balance shown in red ink is below zero; red also suggests a left-wing protest over conscription

explanation.surface: Communists march in a protest rally.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a protest, it is a red rally over the draft; read as banking, red figures mean money owed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank debit shown in red means more withdrawn than is held in the account.

clue.text: Jerome, old Irish soldier

explanation.surface: A man named Jerome served as a soldier in old Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerome Kern was the American composer of Show Boat; also a light-armed medieval Irish foot soldier.

clue.text: Tricky play by the lady from Helsinki ?

explanation.surface: A woman from Finland pulls off a cunning move in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a pun: a woman from Finland is a 'Finn-ess', as a lioness is to a lion.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, an attempt to win a trick with a lower card is a clever manoeuvre; the pun makes a female Finn.

clue.text: The first murder

parts.note: in Genesis, Cain kills his brother Abel, the first killing recorded

explanation.surface: The original murder in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The killing of one's own brother, as Cain did to Abel.

clue.text: Poet said to be a dandy

indicators.note: said signals the clue word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Beau Nash was a famous Georgian dandy of Bath

explanation.surface: A poet who is reputed to be a fop.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Nashe was an Elizabethan writer and satirist.

clue.text: Numb centre under back bone

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits under the first

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

indicators.note: centre picks the middle letters of the word Numb

explanation.surface: A numbness in the middle of the lower back bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The breastbone, the flat bone at the front of the chest.

clue.text: Old song-books found by theologian in sea-trip

indicators.note: the theologian goes inside the jumbled sea
trip suggests the word sea stumbles into a new order

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

explanation.surface: Ancient songbooks are found by a cleric on a cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Norse collections of mythological and heroic poetry.

clue.text: In favour of church militant body ?

parts.note: for means supporting, in favour of
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A militant group professes support for the church.
explanation.definitionFit: An army, police or armed unit is a body of people organised for action.

clue.text: Communications altered date for anchorage

parts.note: roads are means of communication between places

indicators.note: the letters of the word date are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Messages arrive to say the date has been changed for mooring.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheltered stretch of water off a shore where ships may ride at anchor.

clue.text: Corrects last word in printing measures

indicators.note: the last word sits inside the printing measures

parts.note: ems are units of measure in printing
the end is the final word, the conclusion

explanation.surface: A typesetter fixes the final word in the printed measures.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise text by removing errors is to amend or put it right.

clue.text: Perhaps Ned's near European battle area

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters may be arranged otherwise

parts.note: the name with its possessive s supplies its letters

explanation.surface: Ned's place is close to a European battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: This forested upland in Belgium and Luxembourg saw major fighting in both World Wars.

clue.text: Bird is to cut drink

parts.note: to shear is to cut, as with wool
water is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone is told to cut the drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A seabird of the petrel family that skims low over waves.

clue.text: Lengthy drama includes a monster

indicators.note: the phrase Lengthy drama contains the letters within it

explanation.surface: A long play has a monster in its cast.
explanation.definitionFit: The many-headed serpent of Greek myth slain by Heracles.

clue.text: Possibly each doctor's about to make great sacrifices

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be taken in some other order

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: Every physician is about to make huge sacrifices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a second anagram signal or a link word; the pool is EACH, MBS and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece these were public offerings of many animals, literally a hundred oxen.

clue.text: Occasion on board familiar to rail-travellers.?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: an occasion is a time
a table is a board

explanation.surface: An occasion on a train that commuters know well.
explanation.definitionFit: The schedule of train departures is the thing every railway passenger consults.

clue.text: Old jockey rides horse to East Hertfordshire town

parts.note: Steve Donoghue was a famous English jockey of the 1920s
a nag is a horse
E is east

explanation.surface: A retired jockey rides a horse to a town in Hertfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A new town north of London, in the county of Hertfordshire.

clue.text: Just a worker, this man's the chief assistant

parts.note: right means just, fair
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: This man is merely an employee, yet he is the boss's chief aide.
explanation.definitionFit: One's most trusted helper is called one's right-hand man.

clue.text: River has little periodical rise in general

indicators.note: rise in a down clue makes the letters read upwards

parts.note: the Nile is a river
mag is a short form of magazine

explanation.surface: A river rises a little periodically in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Gamelin was the French commander-in-chief in 1940.

clue.text: English composer's address by French river

parts.note: M. abbreviates Monsieur, a form of address
Thomas Arne, English composer of Rule, Britannia, with the possessive

explanation.surface: An English composer gives his address beside a river in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A river of north-east France, famous for First World War battles.

clue.text: Girl sees nothing in poor Barret

indicators.note: nothing goes inside the scrambled name
poor suggests the name Barret is in bad shape and rearranged

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A girl sees no merit in a poor Barret.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, the feminine of Robert.

clue.text: His name even before being toasted at school

definitions.text: His name even before being toasted at school

parts.words: His name even before being toasted at school
parts.note: the hero of a Victorian school novel is roasted before the fire by a bully; his surname means toasted

explanation.surface: A boy is named before being toasted by bullies at school.
explanation.walkthrough: In Thomas Hughes's Rugby School novel the hero is held before the fire by Flashman; his surname is a word for toasted.
explanation.definitionFit: The schoolboy hero of Tom Brown's Schooldays is the boy roasted at Rugby.

clue.text: Daily they proverbially change

explanation.surface: A newspaper says things never stay the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A London daily newspaper; and the age or era that the saying says always alters.

clue.text: Send a metronome up

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters go upwards

parts.note: a metronome is a timer for musicians

explanation.surface: Mail a metronome upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to send money or a matter onward.

clue.text: Firm with representative in Derby, perhaps.

explanation.surface: A company has a delegate at a racecourse event.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is England's most famous flat horse race; racing yards enter horses in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm means steady, unshakeable; a racing yard has a runner in the Epsom race.

clue.text: Jorrocks's mount — a Greek one

explanation.surface: The horse ridden by Jorrocks is a Greek one.
explanation.walkthrough: Jorrocks is the fox-hunting grocer of R. S. Surtees's comic novels.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek mountain piled on Pelion in myth; mount means mountain, though the surface wants a horse.

clue.text: Eskimo dogs — neither bitches nor barkers

parts.note: dogs that are not bitches are male
dogs that do not bark are mute, silent ones

explanation.surface: Arctic sled dogs that are all dogs and never bark.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerful Alaskan breed of sledge dog with a thick coat.

clue.text: State of the road in SE Asia

definitions.text: State of the road in SE Asia

parts.words: State of the road in SE Asia
parts.note: a country in South-East Asia that gave its name to a famous wartime supply road to China

explanation.surface: A traveller asks about road conditions in South-East Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: This South-East Asian country, now Myanmar, named the wartime supply route into China.

clue.text: Legislator makes change on rates

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A lawmaker alters the local property rates.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a senate, the upper house of a parliament.

clue.text: A border round a middle figure

indicators.note: the border goes round the second a

parts.note: a verge is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A frame drawn round a number in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A mean value is a central or typical figure.
